author: TEDx Talks
description:
Language is part of what makes us human. For the first time in history, artificial models are now using language in sophisticated ways. By exploring how AI learns language, we can uncover new insights into our own learning processes and better appreciate the remarkable flexibility and efficiency of our minds.

Jennifer is an Assistant Professor of Cognitive Science at Johns Hopkins University and a former Research Fellow at Harvard’s Kempner Institute. With a PhD from MIT, her research bridges cognitive science, language, and machine learning to uncover how humans communicate so efficiently. Through computational modeling and experiments, she explores the mind’s inner workings while advancing safe AI—pursuing knowledge that inspires innovation for a brighter, more thoughtful future. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why we’re so good at learning languages (according to AI) | Jennifer Hu | TEDxNewEngland

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world overflowing with information, perhaps the most important skill we are losing is the ability to ask a good question.

In this compelling talk, Prabhu Chawla, one of India's most respected journalists and political commentators, explores the power of questioning as a tool for understanding, accountability, and truth. Drawing from more than four decades in journalism and his experience conducting some of India's most memorable political interviews, he reveals what separates a routine question from one that can challenge power, uncover uncomfortable truths, and change the course of a conversation.

Through insights from his iconic Seedhi Baat interviews and decades of reporting, Prabhu examines how the art of questioning has evolved in an age of soundbites, social media, polarization, and instant information. He asks whether, in our pursuit of quick answers, we have forgotten to pause and ask the questions that truly matter.

Seedhi Baat is an invitation to rediscover the power
title: Seedhi Baat: The Lost Art of Asking The Right Question | Prabhu Chawla | TEDxGGSIPU EDC

description:
Using the shoe as a metaphor, San Ge describes the pursuit of ideals as a journey of continuous sensing and the courage to change shoes. His three pairs of "shoes": The first was the "entrepreneur's shoe"—born of passion but ending in pain—which taught him that pain is the signal to change. The second was the "healer's shoe" that let him soar freely, offering the experience of a life wholly allowed. The third was the "tea master's shoe"—chafing yet grounding—which, through confusion and pain, led him to realize that life's true meaning lies not in finding the ultimate answer or the perfect fit, but in navigating by feeling, illuminating the path with awareness, and possessing the courage to bravely change shoes and keep moving forward when passion, pain, or opportunity arrives. His life can be summarized in three journeys.

The first was building a business with his wife, creating **Zhanfang**—China's first literary-casual travel women's wear brand. While designing and crafting garmen
title: An ideal is a pair of shoes that keeps changing sizes. | Ge San | TEDxSuzhou

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Standing at 17,500 feet in Ladakh, surrounded by clear skies and a view that made him feel like a speck in the universe, Ripudman looked down and saw trash. That moment, he says, defined the next decade of his life. In this talk he traces the path from a high-flying corporate career: six flights a week, five-star hotels, a multinational sales team to bending down on his morning runs to pick up litter, and discovering that this one small act could turn strangers into community and cynicism into action.

He shares the stories that convinced him he was onto something: schoolchildren who cleaned a beach in forty-degree heat, students at a school in Gurgaon who realized cleaning a market wasn't enough until they brought the shopkeepers in, and a village near Udaipur where sharing water equitably slowly dissolved caste divides until a lower-caste farmer led the collective. Along the way he draws a line between the litter on our streets and the litter in our minds — the consumerism, the inst
title: One Planet. One Act. One Piece of Litter. | Ripudaman Singh Bevli | TEDxTSMS Noida Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
From an early age, Komal Singh was cast as "the studious one" top of her class, the cousin every relative held up as the example. But there was always another version of her: the girl who played every sport she could and cried when she got run out at one run, not over the trophy but because she cared that much. In this talk, she traces what happens when the two people you're told to choose between refuse to stay separate.

Her path runs from a good engineering career to a mountain she saw in a movie, to a shin fracture and a diagnosis that ended her dream of climbing before it began. Told her bones might never take the load again, she rebuilt herself one race at a time learning to swim six months before a half Ironman, getting stung by a jellyfish and spraining her leg mid-race but crawling across the finish line, then completing full Ironman races in Australia and Germany, and setting a course record in the Thar Desert.

What she found wasn't a replacement identity but a merged one:
title: Don't Drain One River to Feed Another | Komal Singh | TEDxTSMS Noida Youth

description:
### **Using Social Media in a Positive Way**

**Mr Heng Chee Kuan (Uncle Potato)**

Social media is often criticised for encouraging comparison, conflict and negativity. But what if the same platforms could be used to connect people, mobilise kindness and provide practical help to those who need it most?

Heng Chee Kuan, affectionately known as **“Uncle Potato,”** believes that you do not need to be rich to make a meaningful difference. A florist turned community advocate and charity giver, he has used social media to bring together ordinary people who are willing to contribute their time, skills, resources and compassion to help others.

Through this network of goodwill, Heng provides free or affordable ambulance services for poor and bedridden patients who need transportation to hospitals, free accommodation for financially disadvantaged patients travelling from out of town, and a free call service offering a listening ear to people experiencing emotional distress or suicidal though
title: Using Social Media in a Positive Way | Heng Chee Kuan | TEDxUTAR

author: TEDx Talks
description:
It started with forty tiny rectangles on a laptop screen as a seven-year-old in an online classroom, more curious about the devices his classmates were using than the lesson itself. In this talk, Abhimanyu traces how one banned video game turned him from someone who wanted to play games into someone who wanted to build them, and how a single habit of asking questions further carried him from video editing to coding to robotics to cybersecurity.

Along the way he breaks a favourite remote-control car just to understand how it worked, builds an award-winning vertical-farming system, and lands an internship with the Gurugram Police cyber team as its youngest member. He shows how easily everyday details such as a birthday photo, a school uniform, a visible ID card become a digital footprint, and walks through Project Sentinel Hub, the investigation tool he built to trace a case from a single clue while protecting the people behind the data.

His real message isn't about hacking or hardwar
title: The Next Question Is Yours | Abhimanyu Khera | TEDxTSMS Noida Youth

hat do people who commit crimes really want—and how different are their desires from everyone else’s?

Security, success, recognition, and belonging are universal human needs. Yet the ways people pursue them can lead down very different paths. Drawing on her experiences as a university professor and volunteer police officer in Malaysia, as well as her research involving prisoners and police volunteers, Dr Cheah Phaik-Kin explores how connection and exclusion shape human choices.

Through stories from the field, Dr Cheah reveals that when individuals feel supported, valued, and included, they are more likely to use their strengths in service of others. When they feel rejected or disconnected, however, those same human needs can sometimes lead to harmful decisions.

title: What Criminals Want and Why We Want It Too | Cheah Phaik Kin | TEDxUTAR

description:
Every color, image, font, package, and logo tells us something. But what if design does more than communicate an idea? What if it shapes what we believe, what we desire, and even what we choose?

In this thought-provoking talk, Khushika Pahwa, Founder and Brand Director of Fond of Designs Studio, explores the hidden influence of design in the world around us. Drawing from her experience building brands and working with D2C businesses, she challenges the idea that design is simply about making things look good.

From the brands we trust to the products we choose and the identities we associate with, design quietly constructs narratives and influences perception. Khushika examines how visual language can become a form of persuasion, turning values into symbols and ideas into experiences.

But propaganda isn't always manipulation. It can also be intentional storytelling: a way for brands, creators, and communities to communicate what they stand for and shape how they are understood.

description:
Rivers are destroying our oceans: just 10 rivers carry 80% of the plastic pollution reaching the sea. Anssi Mikola invented a solution to this global crisis, but no one wanted it, not even for free. Join him on a journey from repeated failures and rejection to building a scalable solution with global impact. Anssi Mikola is a Finnish entrepreneur and engineer with more than 30 years of experience building companies across different industries. A few years ago, he set out to tackle river pollution by inventing a device that removes plastic from waterways. The technology worked. The market did not.
Instead of giving up, Anssi changed direction. He stopped trying to sell a machine and began working directly with communities, partners, and local operators. He founded RiverRecycle to turn river waste into usable material while creating local jobs in emerging markets.

title: Becoming the River Cleaner | Anssi Mikola | TEDxVaasa
